description_en: A group ofśikharamonuments from the 14th-15th century.The site lies in the massif of Manilek, some 8 kilometres north east of Amargadhi, the district's headquarter. The monuments are surrounded by terraced fields.The plan of the architectural complex is relatively unique. Twośikharatemples are built in front of one another, on the same masoned stone platform. They are oriented to the east and to the west. A pair of miniatureśikharatemples is erected to the N-E, N-W and S-E of these monuments. The resulting layout is that of apañcāyatana("five altars") plan. In architecture this plan is know aspañcadevala. Interestingly, thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which corresponds to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century (Andolfatto 2022). No otherpañcadevalacomplex has been surveyed so far in far-western Nepal and it is possible to suggest that the miniature temples are in fact later additions.The plan of the two centralśikhara(001 and 002) and the architectural fragments found in situ indicate that a domed pavilion was originally standing between the two temples. This type of plan is found at the nearby sites of Ajayamerukoṭa (DDL0110,DDL0111) and at the Bhurtī Temple Complex, in Dailekh district (DLK0015). There are nevertheless structural differences between the Bhurtī and Ajayamerukoṭa monuments: in Bhurtī the pavilion was built as a planned constituent of the temples (with a supporting capital in the main masonry of the temple), while in Ajayamerukoṭa the pavilion appears as an independant structure. This would indicate that the architects at work in Bhurtī were inspired by pre-existing models, such as the Ajayamerukoṭa monuments (themselves modelled on temples from Uttarakhand). Nevertheless, in Badma Āmtad Deval, the dome was supported by capitals carved out in the masonry, i.e. in the same manner as in Bhurtī.Another unique feature of the two mainśikhara, is the inner circular corbelled dome, which is a technic usually employed for domed pavilions. The dome that connected the two monuments is now completely collapsed. Parts of it, and maybe of other monuments too, were piled up in the two mainśikhara.A fourth pair of miniatureśikharawas probably built to the S-W.The monuments of Badma Āmtad Deval show no visible sign of religious affiliation. They may be dated around the 14th-15th century, i.e. from the time of the Pāla kings of the Doti kingdom.The temples are described inSharma 2012, p. 331-332 (the six miniatureśikharaare omitted from the description).
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2022. “Les temples deval de la Karnali (Népal occidental) : réflexions sur leur datation et leur vocation", Arts Asiatiques , Vo. 76, p. 31-46. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
